name: Weinlokal Stern
description: German classics in a room that feels like a proper Weinlokal.

name: RIJKS
description: Polished, memorable, and firmly in occasion territory.

name: 't Lemmeke
description: Excessively good food — the new go-to in Oud-Zuid we keep booking again.

name: Tacite
description: High-end dining in Oud-Zuid — special-occasion pacing and a serious wine list.

name: De Kas
description: Warm, occasion-worthy, and intimate without feeling stiff.

name: Vermut
description: Hot spot for drinks in Amsterdam-West — also on JP Heijestraat (see Vermouth JP Heijestraat in new openings).

name: Café de Klos
description: Cozy, no-frills Amsterdam classic known for its ribs.

name: MOMO Restaurant
description: Spacious dining room that actually seats bigger parties without feeling chaotic, with a cocktail bar for before or after.

name: Cecconi's Amsterdam
description: Buzzy but manageable for six-plus — big booths, shareable pasta, easy for a crowd.

name: Le Petit Bouillon d'Amsterdam
description: Oeufs mayo, steak frites and a bottle of wine for a low price; the smaller sister of the first Bouillon by Magna Plaza, this time with a terrace.

name: Bolenius
description: Greenhouse produce, elegant plates — a date-night pick for veg-forward eaters.

name: Restaurant 212
description: Counter seats around an open kitchen on the Amstel; precise cooking, strong wines.

name: Wils
description: Open kitchen, Nordic-leaning plates, and a lively but refined room.

name: Zuiver Bar
description: Natural-wine supplier to the city’s restaurants — outgrew the Choux corner and opened their own bar a few doors down. Stock up or stay for a lovingly uncorked glass.

name: Omoka
description: Fridays and Saturdays — head to NDSM for the tastiest African dishes (opposite Botel).

name: Café-Restaurant De Plantage
description: Greenhouse-adjacent dining with a strong vegetable programme.

name: Sinne
description: Relaxed open-kitchen room; Asian flavours through modern European cooking.

name: Rotate
description: From the team behind Jondani — just as polished as Beethovenstraat, now on Leidseplein.

name: Layers
description: The French bakery & deli favourite — now in the center as well as the original neighbourhood spot.

name: Chun
description: Chun's third café, in the Bijenkorf's old pastry shop: Korean-style toasts (the rib-eye bulgogi one sells out), Uji matcha and coffee.

name: Bakers & Roasters
description: Kiwi-style café with a serious brunch menu and plenty of veg options.

name: Pimpelmees
description: Neighbourhood favourite that keeps earning repeat visits.

name: Café Publiek
description: Casual wine bar energy — small plates worth sharing.

name: Café Restaurant De Baanderij
description: A new living room on the IJ at the NDSM shipyard — always buzzing, always a spot, and a menu full of proper dishes.

name: Bakery Wolf Zuidas
description: Location four — the largest Wolf yet, on the Zuidas where the Wild & The Moon site used to be. To-go Rozengracht and Utrechtsestraat, café Wolvenstraat — and now the suits get a proper filled roll too.

name: Bar Staal
description: From the Vooges team — breakfast through late-night snacks on a sun-drenched terrace by the water. Schinkelbuurt staycation energy.

name: Bar How
description: Natural wine bar on Papaverhoek — easy new weekend date spot.

name: Arte Vanilla
description: Homemade gelato to nonna’s recipe — the hot-summer essential.

name: CTaste
description: Dining in the dark — memorable for a group, book well ahead.

name: Vita Lente
description: Back on the radar — relaxed Italian that rewards a slow evening.

name: Café Kompleet
description: Kompleet again on the shortlist — dependable lunch and excellent coffee.

name: Eatery Van Beeren
description: Great value for money with a lovely courtyard — book outside when the weather cooperates.

name: Leauf
description: The little sibling — those richly topped bakery favourites from the original, now in the city center.

name: La Brutal Taquería
description: Mexico City street tacos on the Albert Cuyp — fresh off the press daily, almost forget you’re in Amsterdam.

name: NENI Amsterdam
description: Middle Eastern sharing menu — colourful, fun, and easy for two.

name: Café Susy
description: Worth putting on the list again — easy café energy, good people-watching.

name: Duke of Tokyo
description: Second location in De Pijp — cocktails with a Japanese twist and bar snacks, then warm up your vocal cords in a karaoke booth.

name: The Pancake Bakery
description: Huge tables, savoury and sweet pancakes — easy with kids or a big group.

name: Canvas
description: Event-friendly room with modular seating and a shareable menu.

name: Bon Burgerbar North
description: North-side burger run that still hits when you want something unfussy and loud.

name: Het Broeker Huis
description: Not new, but firmly on the radar — nice and old-school, great value for a bargain night out.

name: Hanneke's Boom
description: Casual terrace on the water — burgers, bitterballen, and a few veg bites.

name: Café Caron
description: Buzzy French bistro: classics with a modern twist, open late.

name: Auberge
description: Generous French bistro cooking, a well-priced set menu, French wines.

name: Utage Sake Bar
description: Easygoing izakaya: small plates to share and a long sake list.

name: Toet
description: Relaxed open-kitchen spot by the RAI, modern Mediterranean plates.

name: De Juwelier
description: Vintage-feel bistro with an open kitchen; French classics at fair prices.

name: Veneur
description: Old-school French bistro with open-fire cooking and a terrace.

name: EN
description: Lively Japanese, traditional and creative plates, with a deep sake list.

name: Visaandeschelde
description: Long-running seafood brasserie: oysters, fish classics, nautical room.

name: Ciel Bleu
description: Creative tasting menus on the hotel's top floor, with views over the city.

name: Bistro de la Mer
description: Parisian-style bistro bringing back old fish recipes, with a serious wine list.

name: Zoldering
description: Lively neighbourhood bistro: bold French flavours and standout wine service.

name: Yamazato
description: Traditional kaiseki with ingredients flown in from Japan.

name: Showw
description: Elegant, lounge-like room with modern cooking and sommelier-led wines.

name: Flore
description: Two stars plus a Green Star — produce-first tasting menu by the Amstel.

name: CUE
description: Bold, smoky, fermented flavours over a short or long menu, natural wines, then a cellar bar downstairs.

name: Café Restaurant Amsterdam
description: Big, lively brasserie in a 1900 water-pumping hall, serving all-day classics and seafood platters.

name: BAK
description: Seasonal, local tasting menu on the third floor of a harbour warehouse looking out over the IJ.

name: Hotel de Goudfazant
description: Not a hotel: a French-leaning three-course menu served in a vast old warehouse by the IJ.

name: Troef
description: Neo-bistro in an old workshop, with refined French-leaning plates and a very deep wine list.

name: Restaurant Blauw
description: Modern Indonesian known for its rijsttafel, a long spread of small dishes, including a vegan one.

name: Choux
description: Vegetable-led tasting menus with house ferments, in an old industrial building by the IJ.

name: Alba
description: Relaxed natural-wine spot with a rotating set menu of bold, creative plates, also served à la carte.

name: Helling 7
description: Open-fire cooking in a rebuilt shipyard hall at NDSM, with a terrace on the IJ and a veg chef's menu.

name: Vinkeles
description: Two-star French cooking with rich, layered sauces, in the old bakery of an 18th-century canal-side almshouse.

name: Bougainville
description: Intimate fine-dining room over Dam Square, mixing French technique with Asian and Middle Eastern spice.

name: MOS
description: Creative French-leaning tasting menus, with a full vegetarian version, at the tip of the IJdok over the water.

name: Lars Amsterdam
description: French technique with Asian accents by the harbour, plus a plant-based menu grown in its own rooftop garden.

name: Restaurant Europa
description: Inventive, seafood-leaning tasting menu served along a 25-metre counter facing the open kitchen.

name: Toscanini
description: Jordaan stalwart since 1985 for regional Italian cooking, fresh pasta and house-baked bread.

name: Wilde Zwijnen
description: Modern Dutch cooking from seasonal, regional produce, with a vegetarian set menu, on Javaplein.

name: Barracuda
description: Unfussy fish canteen in an old Noord workshop: tick off shared plates of the day's catch and shellfish.

name: Café Parlotte
description: Cosy corner wine bistro with a weekly-changing three-course menu and a long, French-leaning wine list.

name: Thai Thai Poppetje
description: Lively Thai street-food bar known for khao soi and Isaan salads, with tofu or jackfruit swaps on most dishes.

name: Café de Klepel
description: Snug French wine café with a daily three- or four-course bistro menu and more than 300 French bottles.

name: Roest
description: Big industrial hall on Oostenburg with fire-cooked bistro dishes, a summer terrace and DJs on Fridays.

name: REM
description: Restaurant and rooftop bar on a former pirate-radio sea platform, with chef's menus over the IJ and seasonal cocktails up top.

name: Wijmpje Beukers
description: Relaxed eetcafé with a short seasonal menu, serious cocktails and tables kept free for walk-ins.

name: Scheepskameel
description: Straightforward Dutch cooking and a huge wine list in an old naval-yard building on Kattenburg.

name: Gitane
description: All-day neighbourhood café-restaurant: brunch, then Mediterranean-leaning plates and natural wines.

name: Bridges
description: Polished fish-focused restaurant in Sofitel The Grand, with French tasting menus and a vegetable menu.

name: Vermeer
description: Intimate hotel dining room serving French-rooted sharing plates built on Dutch produce.

name: Daalder
description: Dennis Huwaë's refined six-course dinner, back in its original corner spot on the Lindengracht.

name: Kaagman & Kortekaas
description: Lively open-kitchen restaurant with a seasonal set menu built around game, fish and wild greens.

name: Gebr. Hartering
description: Busy brothers-run bistro serving a daily-changing table d'hôte menu from small local suppliers.

name: Rijsel
description: Bustling French-Flemish bistro in a former domestic-science school, at fair prices.

name: VanOost
description: Fine dining in a lofty 1908 university building, blending French technique with Japanese flavours.

name: De Mark
description: Wood-fired, vegetable-led seasonal cooking in a dike-side hotel in Durgerdam village.

name: Gertrude
description: Oud-West bistro of seasonal sharing plates. Get the hamachi and the shrimp and bone-marrow dumpling.

name: Trees
description: Zeedijk bistro with a cocktail bar below. Order oysters, steak tartare or sole meunière, then go downstairs for a drink.

name: Ikkoku
description: Counter omakase cooked over an irori fire, hidden behind a matcha bar. Bluefin tuna or A5 wagyu courses.

name: Sjefietshe
description: Small corner ceviche bar in De Pijp. Order a few ceviches, the tuna tataki and the octopus roll.

name: De Japanner
description: Late-night izakaya on the Albert Cuyp. Share gyoza, bao, crispy rice and beef tataki.

name: Singel 404
description: Small canal-side lunch café, here since 1996. Order the tuna melt on sourdough or the Singel club.

name: Brasserie Zuiderbad
description: Simple café inside the 1912 Zuiderbad pool building near the Rijksmuseum. Sandwiches, bitterballen and fries.

name: Groot Melkhuis
description: Self-service park café by the water with a big playground. Get a baguette, the pea soup or the cheeseburger.

name: Café-Restaurant Hesp
description: Old brown café on the Amstel with a big terrace. Desembrood sandwiches at lunch, chicken saté or bavette at dinner.

name: Café de Schreierstoren
description: Café in the 15th-century city-wall tower by Centraal. Dutch pancakes, a croquette sandwich or chicken saté.

name: Landmarkt
description: Farm-shop restaurant in Schellingwoude using market produce. Eggs Benedict, the soup of the week or the swordfish Niçoise.

name: Tashi Deleg
description: Tibetan and Indonesian kitchen on the Utrechtsestraat. Order the rijsttafel or Tibetan momos.

name: Sampurna
description: Long-running Indonesian on the Singel by the Flower Market. Share a rijsttafel or try the goat saté and rendang.

name: Café Jakarta
description: Hotel restaurant at the tip of Java-eiland with IJ views. Order the Tafel Jakarta tasting or the beef rendang.

name: Blue Pepper
description: Modern Indonesian with a coursed rijsttafel. Go for 'The Sultan and I' menu or the beef rendang.

name: Waterkant
description: Busy Surinamese spot on the canal by the Marnixstraat garage. Chicken roti roll, heri heri or a bakkeljauw bun.

name: Roopram Roti
description: No-frills Surinamese roti shop in the Dapperbuurt. Get roti kip or roti lam.

name: Haven van Texel
description: Dutch eetcafé with a terrace on the canal at the Zeedijk end. Order the pea soup and the stamppot.

name: Café de Blaffende Vis
description: Brown café near the Noordermarkt since around 1916. Uitsmijter at lunch, chicken saté or the burger at dinner.

name: De Oceaan
description: Small harbourside eetcafé in the Eastern Docklands with a waterside terrace and SUP rental.
address: R J H Fortuynplein 29, 1019 WL, Amsterdam

name: Captein & Co
description: Eetcafé on the Oudeschans with a canal terrace. Bitterballen to start, then chicken saté or trout.

name: Chez van Rijn
description: Parisian-style brasserie on Rembrandtplein with live jazz. Onion soup, then steak frites or coq au vin.

name: Spanjer en van Twist
description: Canal-side restobar on the Leliegracht now cooking Chilean food. Try the empanada, pastel de choclo or costillar.

name: Pension Homeland
description: Hotel, brewery and restaurant in the old officers' mess on the Marineterrein. Crab bisque, then steak with béarnaise.

name: Khorat Top Thai
description: Long-standing neighbourhood Thai near Vondelpark. Tom kha kai, fish cakes and a curry.

name: Ron Gastrobar
description: Ron Blaauw's lively starred gastrobar in Zuid with small and large plates. Order the beef Wellington and the boneless spareribs. Closing February 2027.

name: Siam Bowl
description: Thai street-food noodle bar with plastic stools. Order the khao soi, or tom yum noodles if you like it hot and sour.

name: Bird
description: Busy Chinatown Thai with a long menu, open since 1998. Go for a green or red curry and expect a short wait at the bar.

name: Songkran
description: Small family-run Thai with 28 wines. Try the Thai fish cakes and the chef's dorade specials.

name: Maenaam Thai
description: Simple, low-priced Thai near Spui. Order the pad thai or the massaman curry.

name: Warie's Thai Food
description: Small Thai with an open kitchen and a terrace, opposite the fire station. Order the green curry or pla sam rod.

name: Bangkok
description: Family-run Thai behind Tuschinski, open late. Start with the mixed starter, then pad thai or a curry.

name: Ocha
description: Tiny Thai room near Nieuwmarkt run by the same two cooks for years. Order the red curry with bamboo.

name: Boi Boi
description: Lao and Thai cooking by a chef who learned from his grandmother. Try the zin tod beef jerky and the laab.

name: Little Thai Prince
description: Small, plain Thai on the Zeedijk. Reviewers rate the tom yum soup, red curry and fried noodles.

name: Krua Buppha
description: Neighbourhood Thai on lower Van Woustraat with dishes that aren't too sweet. Book ahead, it fills up.

name: Cookkai
description: Tiny Thai snackbar and takeaway in the Jordaan since 2001. Order the keang karrie kai or the pad thai.

name: Kinnaree
description: Steady Jordaan Thai with a broad menu of soups, curries and wok dishes.

name: Krua Thai Classic
description: Family-run Thai near Waterlooplein since 1991, one of the city's first. Order the green curry or panang.

name: Sawaddee Ka
description: Thai on Overtoom with more than 100 dishes on the menu. Order a red curry or the house pad thai with beef.

name: Phu Thai
description: Isaan family cooking, mostly takeaway with a few tables. Order the beef laab or the beef noodle soup.

name: Royal Thai
description: Long-running Thai off Leidseplein, open late, with its own vegetarian starters and mains.

name: Baibua
description: Small family-run Thai eethuis off Vijzelstraat. Try the green papaya salad and the curries.

name: Rakang
description: Bangkok-style dishes for sharing in the Jordaan since 1994. Order a few plates, like panang beef and chicken in pandan leaf.

name: Cornerstore
description: Asian-leaning small plates on the Papaverweg in Noord, with a veg tasting menu, natural wine and good cocktails. Walk in for drinks, with music late into the night.

name: Copain
description: Seasonal, vegetable-led cooking at NDSM, with a menu that changes theme each season and 4 to 6 course chef's menus. Wine or house kombucha pairings, and it suits a group as well as a date.

name: Café Modern
description: A surprise set menu of 5 to 7 courses in an old bank building on the Meidoornweg. The wine is kept in the bank's vault, which is also a private dining room.

name: Lazuur
description: A French–Portuguese bistro in Nieuwendam with a chef's menu, an almost all-Portuguese wine list and lots of port by the glass. Book by 20:30, and ask first for more than 6.

name: Café Cress
description: Seasonal cooking from market produce on the Johan van Hasseltkade, with a terrace on the water. They import their own organic wines, mostly Riesling, and make good cocktails.

name: Barossa
description: A Peruvian chef cooking Dutch produce on the water at NDSM Marina. You pick four courses plus sides, and groups of 8 or more book by email.

name: Café Restaurant Metro
description: An all-day café with its own bakery by the NXT Museum, serving a flexible 3-course dinner Tuesday to Saturday. Lots of natural wine by the glass, and always a veggie or vegan option.

name: Restaurant V12
description: A 3 or 4 course European menu with two choices a course, in an industrial room with a sunny terrace. Natural wine, small plates, and room for big groups.

name: FC Hyena
description: The restaurant in an arthouse cinema on the IJ. Seasonal plates from a wood-fired oven, natural wine and a terrace on the water, good before or after a film. Walk in, or book for 6 or more.

name: Nikotin
description: Japanese and Korean fusion from the grill on the Hamerkanaal, by Coulisse's former owner. Kimchi, oysters and flatbreads, a €75 set menu, sake and good cocktails, plus a big terrace and private hire for groups. Late and lively at weekends, sometimes with a DJ.

name: Klaproos
description: Wood-oven pizza, fresh pasta and antipasti on the Papaverhoek, with vegan dishes, a long natural wine list and private rooms for groups. Quietest midweek, as it turns into a late bar on Friday and Saturday.

name: Bacalar
description: A taqueria in an old garage in Noord, with tacos and tostadas from a weekly menu, octopus included, a big mezcal collection and cocktails. Sunny terrace, and book ahead at weekends.

name: Moon
description: On the 19th floor of the A'DAM Toren, with views over the IJ and the city. A seasonal chef's menu of four or five courses (€73 or €92.50), plus oysters and bites. One for a special night out.

name: Ryo
description: Japanese and Cantonese on NDSM-Plein, looking out over the IJ. Sushi, dim sum and Cantonese classics made for sharing, and a bar for a drink first. Open every day for lunch and dinner.

name: Vuurtoreneiland
description: Dinner on a tiny island in the IJmeer by Durgerdam, cooked over open fire. The boat leaves from the Lloyd Hotel at 17:30, with a borrel plank on the way out and something sweet on the way back. A six-course set menu, so book well ahead.

name: Pelusa
description: Gastropub on the Leen Jongewaardkade with an Argentinian-style grill. Wild fermented beers, cider and natural wine, a short seasonal menu with a ribeye to share, and good bar snacks. Open late at weekends.

name: Papa Thang
description: Vietnamese street food bistro by chef Thang Pham, with a bit of everywhere else thrown in. Bánh xèo, pho, bun cha and spare ribs, lots of plant-based dishes, and signature cocktails at the bar. Plates for sharing.

name: Bar Karma
description: Karma Kebab's sit-down place on the NDSM-Kade, a few minutes from the ferry. Plant-based Middle Eastern sharing plates from the fire, flatbreads and dips, with a €39 menu where you pick a house special and they bring the rest. Very good for vegans and big tables.

name: Café Warung Pas
description: Homemade Indonesian comfort food upstairs at Noordwal 1, a short walk from the IJplein ferry. Ayam geprek with your pick of chilli level, beef or oyster mushroom rendang, dishes steamed in banana leaf, and a monthly special.

name: Skatecafe
description: A restaurant next to an indoor skate park on the Hamerkanaal. Seasonal small plates to share, natural wine, guest chefs on Thursdays and dancing on Friday and Saturday nights. Only open Thursday to Saturday.

name: Bello Gio's by the River
description: Italian on the NDSM-kade in a loud 70s interior. Family recipes from Lazio to Calabria, crisp pizza, handmade pasta and antipasti, with a three-course menu for €37.50 and good cocktails. Takes groups and events.

name: The Beef Chief
description: Burgers that started out of festival food trucks, ten years at Oedipus and now in the kitchen at Transit, a warehouse with a skate park, a bar and a big sunny terrace. Watching them make the burgers is half the fun. Good for groups.

name: Van de Werf
description: Bar and restaurant by the NDSM ferry, open from breakfast to late. Head chef Vilmos Dohnal (ex-Vermeer) gives European classics his own twist, like kimchi risotto with BBQ sepia. Big bar, terrace and a group menu from nine people.

name: Hangar
description: Big terrace right on the IJ at Aambeeldstraat, with plenty of parking. Bistro food from oysters and steak tartare to bavette and fish of the day, and a busy bar into the night. Good for groups and parties.

name: Fred's Kitchen
description: Asian fusion sharing plates and sushi on the NDSM, under the Kraanspoor. Crispy rolls, gyoza, yakitori and Peking duck pancakes, with a long cocktail list. An upstairs floor for groups and a big sunny terrace.

name: De VerbroederIJ
description: A social café by the ferry to Oost, run with and for the neighbourhood. Middle Eastern plates with lots of vegetarian and vegan dishes, some veg from their own garden, and a big sandy terrace and city beach on the IJ.

name: Noorderlicht
description: A café in a greenhouse-like building on the NDSM waterfront, with a big terrace and a fire on cold days. Easy comfort food, from smashburgers to fish and chips and vegan mains, and a good drinks list with local beer.

name: Akub
description: Palestinian recipes with modern twists in a bright room; try the crunchy mansaf.

name: Julie's
description: Glamorous neighbourhood bistro with cosy booths, lobster soufflé and a cocktail trolley.

name: Caia
description: Fire-cooked sharing plates, natural wine and a record-spinning basement bar on Golborne Road.

name: Petersham Nurseries
description: Italian-leaning garden cooking in a flower-filled greenhouse; dinner Thursday to Saturday only.
address: Church Lane & Petersham Road, TW10 7AB, Richmond

name: Sumi
description: Endo Kazutoshi's lively Japanese spot on Westbourne Grove; robata dishes are the highlight.

name: Wildflowers
description: Produce-led Mediterranean sharing dishes from an open kitchen in Newson's Yard.

name: The Hero
description: Maida Vale pub from The Pelican team; hearty, traditional British cooking.

name: Paulette
description: Cosy, old-school French bistro, dinner-only on weekdays and all day at weekends.

name: Canteen
description: Relaxed Portobello Road Italian from the team behind The Pelican and The Hero.

name: Three Darlings
description: Jason and Irha Atherton's all-day Mediterranean bistro on Pavilion Road.

name: The Waterman's Arms
description: Characterful 1850s Thames-side pub with bright small plates, steaks and blackboard fish.

name: Mazi
description: Buzzy Greek sharing plates and Greek wines off Notting Hill Gate, with two terraces.

name: J.Sheekey
description: Wood-panelled theatreland seafood institution; shellfish platters and the famous fish pie.

name: Sketch, The Gallery
description: Eye-popping art-filled brasserie inside Sketch, serving classic dishes and afternoon tea.

name: The Devonshire
description: Restored Soho pub with Guinness downstairs and a robust British grill room above.

name: Impala
description: Meedu Saad's coal-fired sharing plates mixing Egyptian, Middle Eastern and European flavours.

name: Tamila
description: Bustling Northcote Road Indian with big flavours and a relaxed, lively room.

name: Bao
description: The original of several Bao branches; Taiwanese steamed buns and small plates.

name: Ambassadors Clubhouse
description: Opulent, wood-panelled Indian dining room from the team behind Gymkhana.

name: MOI
description: Vast Japanese grill using British produce; skewers, pork chop and a vinyl wall.

name: Aulis
description: Simon Rogan's twelve-seat chef's counter tucked down a Soho alley; one tasting menu.

name: Bob Bob Ricard Soho
description: Glitzy booths with 'Press for Champagne' buttons and classic British dishes.

name: Mountain
description: Brat team's two-floor Spanish spot; wood fire, sharing plates and whole lobster caldereta.

name: Sucre
description: Argentine-inspired parrilla cooking in a grand former concert hall off Carnaby Street.

name: Donia
description: Warm Filipino cooking in Kingly Court; adobo mushroom croquetas and lechon.

name: Bocca di Lupo
description: Long-loved Soho Italian with a regional menu; best seats at the marble counter.

name: Hawksmoor Spitalfields
description: The original of several London sites; British steaks, sides and serious cocktails.

name: Tower House
description: Wood-fired Mediterranean sharing plates in a restored clock tower by Richmond Bridge.

name: The Barbary Notting Hill
description: Bigger sibling of the Neal's Yard original; North African fire and spice, counter seats.

name: Juno Omakase
description: Six-seat omakase room above Los Mochis; fifteen courses of the day's best fish.

name: The Bird in Hand
description: Neighbourhood pub dining room with Roman-style pizza and Mediterranean sharing plates.

name: The Hawthorn
description: Friendly local pub on Uxbridge Road with a short, often-changing British menu.

name: The Anglesea Arms
description: Pioneering Victorian gastropub near Ravenscourt Park with a seasonal, Mediterranean-leaning menu.

name: The Hawk's Nest
description: Railway-arch bar and garden in Shepherd's Bush Market; sourdough pizza and cocktails.

name: 101 Thai Kitchen
description: Unfussy King Street favourite for fiery Isaan and Southern Thai cooking.

name: Bottarga
description: Greek island sharing plates and seafood on the King's Road.

name: Dean Street Townhouse
description: All-day British dining room in the heart of Soho; known for its Sunday roast.

name: Café Boheme
description: Late-opening Old Compton Street brasserie: steak frites, confit duck and escargots.

name: Hobson's Fish & Chips
description: Sit-down fish and chips with table service; one of a handful of London branches.

name: Punjab
description: Family-run Punjabi restaurant, on Neal Street since 1951.

name: Speedboat Bar
description: Loud, fun Bangkok-Chinatown-style Thai canteen on Rupert Street.

name: KİD
description: Turkish grill on Frith Street: pide, meze, Adana köfte and whole roast kid.

name: Baozi Inn
description: Sit-down Chinese on Romilly Street for baozi, dumplings and noodles.

name: Kaia at The Ned
description: Asian-Pacific counter and bar inside The Ned; poke bowls and grill dishes.

name: Duck & Waffle
description: Round-the-clock dining on the 40th floor; the namesake duck and waffle is a must.

name: Dishoom Covent Garden
description: The original of several London sites; Bombay café classics like black daal and bacon naan.

name: Flat Iron Soho
description: The first of many Flat Iron sites; good-value steak with simple sides.

name: Casa do Frango London Bridge
description: The original of a few London sites; Algarve-style piri-piri chicken in a buzzy room.

name: Heard
description: Jordan Bailey's bookable burger restaurant off Carnaby Street; double smash burgers.

name: Quo Vadis
description: Jeremy Lee's seasonal British cooking in a handsome, long-running Dean Street dining room.

name: Manzi's
description: Seaside-style fish restaurant with a jolly room, oyster hour and monkfish tail.

name: Kolamba
description: Sri Lankan cooking on Kingly Street: curries and hoppers.

name: Marjorie's
description: Parisian-style wine bar and restaurant on Foubert's Place, good for long evenings.

name: Milk Beach Soho
description: Modern Australian restaurant and bar with fire cooking and seafood; brunch at weekends.

name: INKO NITO
description: Lively robata grill with Korean touches on Broadwick Street; good for sharing.

name: Kebab Queen
description: Twelve-seat counter beneath Maison Bab serving a playful kebab tasting menu.
